objective: Advise the minimal correct CW-12 durability/recovery contract for first journal directory-fsync failure plus crash namespace loss.
questions: Does C-AC-25/30/33 or the operating contract require restart to remember a pause after the very first durability operation reports parent-directory fsync failure and a crash loses the only directory entry, despite no durable evidence surviving?

If yes, what is the smallest in-scope design that can distinguish never-paused from lost-pause after restart without modifying TaskRepository/G3/contracts? Evaluate pre-created active marker, dual files, and fail-closed absent-journal binding.

If no, specify the defensible contract: pause returns/records persistence failure and stays closed in the current process, but no crash-recovery guarantee is claimed when the persistence substrate explicitly failed. State what test/gate evidence should replace the impossible modeled assertion.
Separately confirm the correct exact-session/generation/request correlation rule for turn_stop_observed events.
constraints: Read-only advice; no files or workflow state changes; distinguish spec requirement from robustness recommendation and avoid inventing authority.
